episode.title: Bound sensitive and attacker-controlled data at diagnostic boundaries
episode.before: At parent 006ac59a33b60bcd87086b5ddd6afa5abe85e448, the credential-token HTTP failure path read the remote response body and appended it verbatim to the thrown error. Multiple channel diagnostics also interpolated raw response bodies or exception text into stderr, including connection retries, message-send failures, token refresh, malformed gateway messages, WebSocket errors, and inbound-handler failures. Truncating some response bodies with slice limited length but did not neutralize control characters or other unsafe log text.
episode.after: At c1235d8c69fcccadf96609af54ed1e08b72fa7ed, credential-token HTTP failures cancel the unconsumed body and expose only the HTTP status in stderr and the thrown error. Other diagnostics pass remote response bodies and exception messages through the shared log-text sanitizer with explicit bounds before writing them or propagating the final connection error. Tests assert that token failures cannot expose the response body and that injected newline, NUL, and tab characters do not survive a propagated connection error; the slash-command audit test additionally checks ANSI, C1, Unicode line-separator, and bidi-control neutralization.
episode.diff: The change replaces raw or slice-only diagnostic interpolation with bounded sanitizeLogText calls across channel connection, sending, persistence, token-refresh, gateway, WebSocket, reconnect, and handler error paths. It changes the credential-token failure contract from reading and embedding the response body to canceling it and emitting status-only diagnostics. The same commit also contains gateway validation and state-persistence hardening, but those are separate concerns from this sensitive-data-redaction episode.

evidence_units.claim: Commit c1235d8c69fcccadf96609af54ed1e08b72fa7ed is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 6200, with parent 006ac59a33b60bcd87086b5ddd6afa5abe85e448 and changes to QQChannel.ts, api.ts, api.test.ts, and send.test.ts.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0], resolved_commit, parent_commit, changed_files_name_status; git show --stat c1235d8c69fcccadf96609af54ed1e08b72fa7ed

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, connection, sending, token-refresh, gateway, WebSocket, and handler diagnostics directly interpolated exception text or used slice-only response-body truncation; the change routes these dynamic values through sanitizeLogText with a 200-character bound.
evidence_units.source: git diff 006ac59a33b60bcd87086b5ddd6afa5abe85e448 c1235d8c69fcccadf96609af54ed1e08b72fa7ed -- packages/channels/qqbot/src/QQChannel.ts; representative after lines 224, 279, 301, 309, 662, 677, 724, 794, 968, 1060, 1131

evidence_units.claim: The final connection failure is rethrown with a sanitized, bounded message while retaining the original error as its cause.

Remote response bodies and exception messages are sanitized immediately where they cross stderr diagnostic boundaries, covering markdown fallback, send failures, state-write and restore failures, token refresh, malformed gateway messages, WebSocket errors, reconnect failures, and inbound-handler failures.
Before the change, a failed access-token request read the remote body and embedded it in the thrown error; afterward it cancels the body and emits an HTTP-status-only stderr line and exception.
evidence_units.source: git diff 006ac59a33b60bcd87086b5ddd6afa5abe85e448 c1235d8c69fcccadf96609af54ed1e08b72fa7ed -- packages/channels/qqbot/src/api.ts; after lines 37-40

evidence_units.claim: The access-token error path preserves actionable HTTP status while deliberately excluding the response payload from both the operator diagnostic and the thrown error.
The token failure test supplies a body named unauthorized-body and requires an exact status-only thrown message, so reintroducing the body would fail the assertion.
The final connection retry test injects newline, NUL, and tab characters into an error and asserts that none survive in the propagated message while readable non-control content remains.

The slash-command audit test verifies that ANSI escape, C1 controls, Unicode line separator, and bidi override characters do not survive the diagnostic line, and that an embedded newline is rendered visibly rather than creating an extra log entry.
The access-token function is called with application credentials by the channel token-fetch path, making its remote failure payload a credential-adjacent diagnostic boundary.

candidate_atomics.name: sanitize-untrusted-diagnostic-text
candidate_atomics.title: Sanitize and bound untrusted diagnostic text
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize remote payloads and exception messages at logging or propagated-error boundaries so control characters cannot forge diagnostics and output size is bounded while readable context remains.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent attacker-controlled response and error text from injecting, reordering, or excessively expanding operator diagnostics while retaining useful readable context.
semantic_action.pre_state: A diagnostic or propagated error is about to include text derived from a remote response, gateway message, user-triggered handler, filesystem error, or other exception whose content is not trusted.
semantic_action.post_state: Every included dynamic text field has passed through the shared log sanitizer with an explicit maximum length; raw line-breaking and control characters do not reach the diagnostic sink.
semantic_action.validation: Inject control-bearing error or command text and assert that newline, NUL, tab, ANSI, C1, Unicode line-separator, and bidi-control characters cannot alter the diagnostic structure, while ordinary readable fragments remain.

candidate_atomics.name: omit-sensitive-remote-error-body
candidate_atomics.title: Replace sensitive remote error bodies with bounded metadata
candidate_atomics.description: Do not read or propagate a remote response body on a credential-adjacent failure when status metadata is sufficient for diagnosis; drain or cancel the body and report only the status.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent server-controlled or secret-bearing response payloads from entering logs and exception messages without eliminating the failure signal needed by operators and callers.
semantic_action.pre_state: A credential-bearing HTTP request has failed and the implementation can observe transport metadata without exposing the response payload.
semantic_action.post_state: The response body is not included in stderr or the thrown error; the body is drained or canceled and the failure retains bounded status metadata.
semantic_action.validation: Return a failed response containing a recognizable sentinel body and require an exact status-only error message that cannot match if the sentinel is appended.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-diagnostic-non-disclosure-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Verify diagnostic non-disclosure and structural safety
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise diagnostic boundaries with recognizable sensitive payloads and control characters, then assert both non-disclosure and preservation of safe troubleshooting context.

semantic_action.intent: Provide regression oracles that fail when sensitive payloads are reintroduced or untrusted text can reshape diagnostic output.
semantic_action.pre_state: Diagnostic boundaries have a defined policy for omitted payloads and sanitized dynamic text.
semantic_action.post_state: Automated tests demonstrate that forbidden response content and structural control characters are absent while allowed status or readable text remains.
semantic_action.validation: Use exact-match assertions for status-only failures and adversarial strings for control-character paths; assert forbidden content is absent and permitted diagnostic context is present.

candidate_workflows.name: harden-sensitive-diagnostic-boundaries
candidate_workflows.title: Harden diagnostics that may contain sensitive or attacker-controlled data
candidate_workflows.description: Choose omission for credential-adjacent response payloads, sanitize and bound dynamic text that must remain useful, and lock both policies down with adversarial regression tests.

workflow_graph.goal: Preserve actionable failure diagnostics without exposing remote sensitive payloads or allowing untrusted text to forge or corrupt diagnostic records.
when_to_use: An HTTP, messaging, gateway, persistence, or handler failure can place remote payloads or exception text into logs or caller-visible errors.
A credential-bearing request currently includes its remote error body in diagnostics.
User-controlled or server-controlled text can contain line breaks, terminal controls, invisible separators, bidi controls, or unbounded content.
anti_goals: Do not remove stable status codes or ordinary readable context needed to diagnose the failure.
Do not treat simple truncation as sufficient protection against control-character or line-forging attacks.
Do not log credential-adjacent response bodies merely because they may contain a useful server error message.
Do not change transport behavior, retry policy, or unrelated state-persistence semantics as part of the redaction contract.
not_applicable_when: The diagnostic contains only fixed application-authored text and bounded trusted scalar metadata.
The response payload is an explicitly approved, schema-validated diagnostic field with a separate disclosure policy and no sensitive content.
No implementation or test boundary exists where the suspected data reaches logs, exceptions, traces, or other diagnostics.
inputs: Inventory of diagnostic sinks and propagated error boundaries
Provenance of each dynamic diagnostic field
Sensitivity policy for remote response bodies
Shared text sanitizer and maximum output lengths
Test harness capable of capturing diagnostics or inspecting thrown errors
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one diagnostic boundary emits a remote response body or unsanitized exception/user-controlled text, creating disclosure or diagnostic-injection risk.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Credential-adjacent bodies are omitted, remaining untrusted diagnostic text is sanitized and bounded at each sink, useful stable metadata remains, and adversarial tests enforce both non-disclosure and structural safety.

steps.condition: Apply when a failed credential-bearing or otherwise sensitive request exposes a remote response body and status metadata is sufficient.
steps.validation: A sentinel response body is absent from an exact status-only error while the HTTP status remains present.

steps.condition: Apply at every diagnostic or propagated-error boundary that must retain dynamic remote, user-controlled, or exception text.
steps.validation: All such fields pass through the shared sanitizer with explicit bounds; no raw dynamic interpolation or slice-only substitution remains at the scoped sinks.

steps.condition: Run after the diagnostic policies are implemented.
steps.validation: Exact-body-leak and adversarial-control tests pass while asserting that safe status and readable context are preserved.

validation_ladder: Diff review: enumerate each scoped dynamic diagnostic interpolation and classify it as omitted or sanitized and bounded.
Focused unit oracle: supply a recognizable remote error body and require exact status-only output.
Adversarial text oracle: inject newline, NUL, tab, ANSI, C1, Unicode separator, and bidi-control characters and assert diagnostic structure is unchanged.
Utility-preservation oracle: confirm stable status codes and ordinary readable error fragments remain available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the data provenance or disclosure policy cannot establish whether a payload must be omitted or may be sanitized and retained.
Stop if no diagnostic sink or propagated-error call site can be established from implementation evidence.
Do not claim completion if tests only check truncation and do not assert absence of sensitive sentinels or structural control characters.
Defer broader coverage claims when changed call sites lack direct adversarial tests.
unresolved_or_deferred: The commit applies sanitization at many call sites, but the added tests directly exercise only selected paths; exhaustive per-call-site runtime coverage is not established.
No test execution result or CI status was available in the evidence bundle, so the changed tests are treated as committed validation oracles rather than observed passing validation.
The shared sanitizer implementation predates this change; this episode establishes its application at new diagnostic boundaries rather than introducing the sanitizer itself.

unresolved_questions: GitHub PR body, reviews, comments, timeline, and status-check results were unavailable in the supplied bundle.
The pinned checkout's working tree contains mass deletions, so tests were not executed; evidence was read directly from pinned and parent git objects without modifying the checkout.

The commit also hardens gateway validation and state persistence, but those concerns were excluded from the candidate workflow because the requested routing class is sensitive-data redaction in diagnostics.
